utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Good morning to everyone. Madam Registrar, would you please call the case.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Good morning, Your Honours. This is the case IT-09-92-T, the Prosecutor versus Ratko Mladic.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Thank you, Madam Registrar. No preliminaries. Therefore, could the witness be escorted into the courtroom. Ms. D'Ascoli, the Chamber has carefully considered the way in which you have conducted the examination-in-chief and grants you another five minutes to conclude. Then I also use the time -- yes. During the testimony - and I'm addressing primarily the Defence - during the testimony of Rupert Smith on the 24th of January, transcript pages 7362 and 63, the Prosecution tendered four documents through the bar table following initial objections from the Defence for them to be admitted as associated exhibits. The Defence was invited to make submissions on the bar table request by the end of the 25th of January, and the four documents were MFI'd as P802 through P805.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: The Chamber seeks the Defence's position on admission of these documents. Good morning, Mr. Nakas. Can you hear me in a language you understand.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I do, yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: I'd like to remind you that you're still bound by the solemn declaration you have given at the beginning of your testimony. Ms. D'Ascoli will now continue her examination. Ms. D'Ascoli.

utterances.speaker: MS. D'ASCOLI
utterances.text: Thank you, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: MS. D'ASCOLI
utterances.text: Good morning, Dr. Nakas.

utterances.speaker: BAKIR NAKAS [Resumed]
utterances.text: Good morning.

utterances.speaker: MS. D'ASCOLI
utterances.text: Can we please have on the screen 65 ter 14298. And can we go to page 83. Dr. Nakas, the one that will appear now on the screens is a photo of a deceased person, Vehid Komar, who is registered among the people who died at the Markale market incident on the 28th of August, 1995. I will just ask that you look at the photo. We now have it on the screen. You can see it clearly; right?

utterances.speaker: BAKIR NAKAS [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. D'ASCOLI
utterances.text: Can we please go quickly go to the next page, page 84, because there's a second photo related to this same person but it's just for a second for -- for it to be visualized. Yes, this is again the same person. And my main question would be on page 83, so if we can go back to the previous page, please. Dr. Nakas, yes, I just wanted you to have a look at this photo and if you can tell us anything about the causes of death of this person just by looking at this photo?

utterances.speaker: BAKIR NAKAS [Resumed]
utterances.text: By looking at this photo, I could practically say nothing about this person's cause of death because there are no visible outside traces of injuries, at least not in this photograph.

utterances.speaker: MS. D'ASCOLI
utterances.text: Okay. Can we now have on the screen, the documented marked with ID, or 65 ter, I'm not sure, 1D00567. And again, Dr. Nakas, once the photo appears on the screen, I will just ask you to have a look at the photo. We see that there is a date on the photo, the 28th of August, 1995. Therefore, you know, the same incident at Markale market. Again, Dr. Nakas, just by looking at this photo, are you able to tell us anything about what is marked with the red circles on the body of this person.

utterances.speaker: BAKIR NAKAS [Resumed]
utterances.text: There are two markings on the body of this person. One is on the edge of the thorax, on the left side, and the other one is on the left upper leg. These are the two signs. They are not telling me anything at the moment. The first one could be a mole. The second one could be the damage on the trousers or it could be a stabbing wound or some other sort of injury but there's no blood. So practically, once again, it would be more imagination if one wanted to describe it as having to do with any injuries.

utterances.speaker: MS. D'ASCOLI
utterances.text: If -- if these were wounds would -- would this type -- these of wounds would be recorded or noted in an autopsy report, even if there were not related to the cause of death of the victim?

utterances.speaker: BAKIR NAKAS [Resumed]
utterances.text: The autopsy report implies that the body is described on the outside, including all the changes that are noticeable whether they are injuries or not. So if there was any injury it would be included. And a different autopsy is the one where cavities are opened. But, in this case, it is obvious that the body is intact. It is only possible to note -- or, rather, make a description of injuries that can be visible on the outer part of the body.

utterances.speaker: MS. D'ASCOLI
utterances.text: And can I ask you whether this type of signs or wounds, if they were wounds, could be caused by -- could have been inflicted by either small pieces of shrapnel or small gun-fire arms, small bullets?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Ms. D'Ascoli, there are several ifs in your question. "If this is a wound, could it be caused by...," that's of course a question no person -- because if it's not a wound, then, of course, it could not be caused by. We do not know -- the witness at least told us that he doesn't know whether it's a mole or a wound or whatever. So it's of no use to further explore this. And then there was even a second if in your first question, "if it is a wound" and "if it is unrelated to the cause of death," there there are two ifs which really any answer would be pure speculation. Please proceed.

utterances.speaker: MS. D'ASCOLI
utterances.text: Okay. I'll move on, Your Honours. Can I now have on the screen the provisional exhibit number P703. And can we please have e-court page 17 in the B/C/S and in the English of this document. This is a set of autopsy reports prepared by the forensic institute of the Faculty of Medicine in Sarajevo concerning victims of the Markale shelling on the 28th of August, 1995.

utterances.speaker: MS. D'ASCOLI
utterances.text: Dr. Nakas, I can see the document is already on the screen. Do you remember viewing this set of autopsy reports?

utterances.speaker: BAKIR NAKAS [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. D'ASCOLI
utterances.text: If you -- if we look at this -- the autopsy report here on the screen, this is an autopsy report of Vehid Komar who is the same person I showed you the photo about. This was the very first photo, page 83 of 65 ter 14298. We see the cause of death is inchibitio psychyca that we read on this report. I just wanted to ask you whether this would be compatible with the photo that you observed before, the very first photo of the body?

utterances.speaker: BAKIR NAKAS [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. The first and last name of the person correspond. This is obvious. And what also corresponds is that there is no claim in the diagnosis that this is an injury sustained from fire-arms but, rather, the causes of death is inchibitio psychyca.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Ms. D'Ascoli, time is over.

utterances.speaker: MS. D'ASCOLI
utterances.text: Okay. Then I just seek to tender the two photos at pages 83 and 84 of 65 ter 14298 confer registrar.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: You would have to upload them separately in order to have the photographs separately being admitted, Ms. D'Ascoli.

utterances.speaker: MS. D'ASCOLI
utterances.text: Yes, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Once that's done, we'll hear from you, and then we'll ...

utterances.speaker: MS. D'ASCOLI
utterances.text: Yes, we will upload it as a separate 65 ter number. And ... can I proceed --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: [Overlapping speakers] ... If there were any technical problems, I hope that they are resolved.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] It is a bit better now. The audibility wasn't really well, so I had to hold the headphones with my hands.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. If you have any further problems, let us know. If not ... Mr. Stojanovic [Realtime transcript read in error "Ms. Stewart"] are you ready to cross-examine the witness.

utterances.speaker: MS. D'ASCOLI
utterances.text: Yes, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes, Ms. D'Ascoli.

utterances.speaker: MS. D'ASCOLI
utterances.text: Sorry, Your Honours. I just wanted to show the witness the document chart to have him affirm that it corresponds to -- you know, [Overlapping speakers]... comments.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. That's -- yes. That's, of course, all -- you should have started with, if you know that you have little time. But I allow you to do that, and that is then the last issue.

utterances.speaker: MS. D'ASCOLI
utterances.text: Thank you, Your Honours. It would really be just the one question.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes, please.

utterances.speaker: MS. D'ASCOLI
utterances.text: Can I please have on the screen 65 ter 28718. And can we go directly -- to page 2 of this document.

utterances.speaker: MS. D'ASCOLI
utterances.text: Dr. Nakas, do you -- do you recognise this chart? And is this the chart where you commented upon a set of medical records that were shown to you in -- in giving your comments about both authenticity and other substantive matters related to the document?

utterances.speaker: BAKIR NAKAS [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. This is the table, and it is also confirmed by my signature next to each place where it says "yes."

utterances.speaker: MS. D'ASCOLI
utterances.text: And does this chart accurately reflect your observations and comments regarding the documents you reviewed? Did you have the opportunity to review the chart and confirm your comments.

utterances.speaker: BAKIR NAKAS [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. D'ASCOLI
utterances.text: Thank you, Dr. Nakas. I don't have further questions.

utterances.speaker: MS. D'ASCOLI
utterances.text: Thank you, Your Honours, for your patience. I will postpone the tendering of this chart until after cross-examination to give the Defence an opportunity to address it.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes, thank you, Ms. D'Ascoli. One small correction to the transcript, page 6, line 10, Ms. Stewart you might be surprised by reading that I asked you whether you were ready for cross-examination. It was Mr. Stojanovic. Mr. Stojanovic, now are you ready to cross-examine the witness?

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Good morning, Your Honours. I hope I am.

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Good morning, Doctor.

utterances.speaker: BAKIR NAKAS [Resumed]
utterances.text: Good morning.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Nakas, you will now be cross-examined by Mr. Stojanovic and Mr. Stojanovic is counsel for Mr. Mladic.

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: Doctor, considering yesterday's examination-in-chief you have made it an obligation for me to ask you a few questions relating to your yesterday's evidence. If I'm not mistaken, this is the fifth time you're appearing before this Tribunal. Am I right?

utterances.speaker: BAKIR NAKAS [Resumed]
utterances.text: It is the sixth appearance but the fifth case because in the first cases I had to appear two times because there was a break.

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: All right. Will you tell me whether in any of the previous cases you mentioned the incident related to the man called Dragan Kalinic.

utterances.speaker: BAKIR NAKAS [Resumed]
utterances.text: I mentioned that incident in the Radovan Karadzic case in my comment when we discussed the relationships in Sarajevo at the time and why certain shellings occurred, and we also discussed some facts that were obvious. I hadn't mentioned him earlier because I did not have any evidence, nor was I personally convinced in this. It was just a rumour and considering that I would be re-telling rumours, then I would just be a messenger, a transmitter. However, at that particular moment I felt the need to say that and it was mentioned for the first time in the Karadzic case.

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: What was it that convinced you that the story you had heard earlier corresponds to the truth?

utterances.speaker: BAKIR NAKAS [Resumed]
utterances.text: What convinced me was that in discussion with my colleagues, when I had returned, this was confirmed when they told me that they had heard the same thing. There was also something that I couldn't find. It was from the Vecernje Novi newspaper that also included the same claim.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Stojanovic, could you assist us in guiding us to certain portions in the statement.

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] The witness says nothing about that in his statement. It's from the examination-in-chief, from yesterday, this is why I started with that. And I said that when I formulated the question. I apologise.

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: Let us return to what you said yesterday. A document was presented to you and that was what Dragan Kalinic said at one of the assembly meetings, and he said what you told us here. What I'm interested in is whether you remember if that had to do with your hospital or rather the Kosevo Hospital.

utterances.speaker: BAKIR NAKAS [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, specifically in that instance it had to do with the Kosevo Hospital, but what was implied was the readiness to shell the Kosevo Hospital and obviously the reciprocity would be valid for any hospital that they considered they had lost at the moment.

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: Would you agree with me that you are now making conclusions, but the military hospital or the General Hospital or the State Hospital in which you worked is not mentioned in his speech. Am I correct?

utterances.speaker: BAKIR NAKAS [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, you are correct. He only says in a description that the employees of the hospital left it and that practically it was left in the enemies' hands, in their view.

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: Thank you. Now I would ask you to look at something from your statement.

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honours, now it is marked as P941.

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: Paragraph 4 of your statement is the one I would like us to have a look at and comment on together, once you see it on the screen in front of you. Paragraph 4 is the one I'm interested in. You say there are --

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Your Honours, just for the record, this document is the under seal.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Not to be shown, therefore, to the public. Please proceed.

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: Paragraph 4, where you say: "However, during my absence from the hospital, I was kept well-informed of everything taking place at the hospital through my brother who was an employee of the hospital and who remained there during most of that period." And my question has to do with this sentence that follows: "I learned that during my absence that the hospital had been targeted at some point in time." What I'd like to know is how did you receive this information and from whom, that in the period between the 8th of April and the 10th of May when you returned to the hospital it had been targeted?

utterances.speaker: BAKIR NAKAS [Resumed]
utterances.text: The information was published in the media, so I could hear it on the TV, and I did. And also in contact with my colleagues, not just my brother, but other colleagues as well. They confirmed to me that they were hit once. I couldn't tell you on what day that was, but it did happen in the relevant period.

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: Would you agree with me that this was the period when the administration of the hospital was still under the control of the Yugoslav People's Army?

utterances.speaker: BAKIR NAKAS [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. Though one should note that it was also obvious in that period in the media reports and it was a well-known thing that snipers were shooting from the roof of the former military hospital, on several occasions, targeting citizens who were moving about the Marin Dvor streets.

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: I will ask you something being that but now please answer my specific question: Who was the head of the hospital at that time, the period you are discussing in paragraph 4 of your statement? Who was the head of the military hospital?

utterances.speaker: BAKIR NAKAS [Resumed]
utterances.text: The then-head of the military hospital was my colleague Colonel Tomislav Tausan, who was a specialist for lung diseases.

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: Please tell us as you have confirmed now what you learned, were you told who targeted the hospital during this period?

utterances.speaker: BAKIR NAKAS [Resumed]
utterances.text: The confirmation of who targeted the hospital is something I did not hear from anyone. It was supposed and commented that members of the TO had targeted it as a response to sniper fire. But that was also just a story going around.

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: When you say "members of the TO," can you please explain what that was and what sort of an abbreviation that is? What does it stand for?

utterances.speaker: BAKIR NAKAS [Resumed]
utterances.text: Members of Territorial Defence, you mean? Those were the forces that wanted to defend the Republic of Bosnia and Herzegovina because there was no organised armed force. We -- there was the reserve police and also reserve Territorial Defence, which was the mainstay of the future Army of Bosnia-Herzegovina.

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: Am I right that Dr. Tausan, as the manager of the hospital, remained in that position practically up until the 10th of May, when the JNA left the hospital?

utterances.speaker: BAKIR NAKAS [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. In fact, yes. They left on the 9th. They went to Lukavica, then returned, spent the night on the hospital premises, and then they left for good on the 10th of May. I don't know whether Dr. Tausan left on the 9th or on the 10th.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Mr. Stojanovic, I just want to find out from the witness. When you say "they left on the 9th," who are the "they"?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] The employees of the former military hospital were, for the most part, members of the Yugoslav People's Army. And some of them were just citizens, ordinary citizens employed by the JNA, but they had also left, some of them, in the convoy which went to Pale via Lukavica. And then further on from Pale in -- I don't know in which direction they continued.

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you. Could we now please have in e-court document 1D778. Your Honours, I must note that we have sent this document for translation. We have not received the translation yet but please allow me to use it. We only have the B/C/S version, so I will use it in a limited way until the moment when we get the official translation.

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: Sir, this is a report on witness interview. The date is the 16th of March, 1996, before the court in Sokolac. And the statement was given by a person you mentioned, Tomislav Tausan.

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Can we please look at the last page of this document now, as it contains the signature. And if we can please zoom in on the signatures.

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: And, Dr. Nakas, please, can you tell me whether you recognise the signature of your former manager, Dr. Tausan?

utterances.speaker: BAKIR NAKAS [Resumed]
utterances.text: This is his full signature. He used to sign his name differently while he was the CEO and one of the doctors. He used his official title, doctor.

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: Thank you. And now let us look at page 2 in this document, paragraph 2. Since we don't have an English translation, I will read from this paragraph to you. It says here that Dr. Tausan, on the 16th of March, 1996, stated, inter alia: "From the very beginning of the war in the former Bosnia-Herzegovina, the military hospital in Sarajevo where I worked was constantly under threat. There was constant sniping and attacks by the Muslim armed forces. Muslim -- the Muslim media launched false information to the effect that JNA members were using the military hospital and opened sniper fire from it on the passers-by, which is absolutely incorrect." I'm asking you in view of what you said in paragraph 4 and then today and what Dr. Tausan said, and he was at the hospital at the time, would you agree with me or, rather, would you agree with Dr. Tausan that his statement is actually correct?

utterances.speaker: BAKIR NAKAS [Resumed]
utterances.text: During the period of time when we were in the hospital together, because it says here "from the very beginning of the war in the former Yugoslavia," around I was in the hospital up to the 8th of April, I did not hear, nor was I informed about any kind of armed forces activity or Muslim forces activity against the military hospital. I was there around the clock. I slept there. And unlike Dr. Tausan, I never experienced fire being opened on the hospital.

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: When you say that --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE FLUEGGE
utterances.text: Mr. Stojanovic, just -- one problem of the record. You didn't indicate where your quotation stopped. And, therefore, in line 17 of page 13, we can read "which is," I think it should read, "absolutely incorrect." Was that part of the quotation, at the end of that paragraph, which I assume is -- would be correct, or is it your comment on this part you read into the record?

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you for your assistance, Your Honours. This is the end of the quotation. My words, "which was absolutely incorrect," was the end of the quotation of paragraph 2 in this statement. Thank you for your assistance.

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: Doctor, I just wanted to hear your impressions, and your impressions are valid up to the 8th of April, when you left the hospital and were not physically present in the hospital before the 10th of May?

utterances.speaker: BAKIR NAKAS [Resumed]
utterances.text: Absolutely. And I can't say that I experienced anything during that period of time because I wasn't there.

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: And now let's look at the same document, paragraph -- or, rather, page 3, paragraph 3, and paragraph 4 as well. Again, I'm going to read those paragraphs out to you, and then I'll have some questions for you. "There was sniping from the Magribija "dzamija" against the hospital. There, the Muslims stored their infantry weapons that they had illegally brought into Sarajevo. I saw when they were bringing in those weapons in a lorry bearing Gorazde registration plates and then used smaller vehicles to transport the weapons from the mosque and distribute it among the Muslims. One of the more fierce attacks was on 26th April, 1992, luckily enough without any casualties." And I continue reading from the following paragraph, another sentence, and I quote: "During one of those fierce attacks against the military hospital which happened on the 3rd of May, 1992, two patients were injured. We informed UNPROFOR about that and we asked for their representatives to come to the site of the incident. However, they never came." My question to you is this: In view of what you stated in paragraph 4, and that is that you had second-hand information, did you ever hear about fire being opened from Magribija, a mosque?

utterances.speaker: BAKIR NAKAS [Resumed]
utterances.text: As for the claim that there was sniper fire from Magribija mosque, I can't say anything because, as you have said it yourself, I wasn't there. However, the claim that that's where infantry weapons were stored and that the weapons had been brought in lorries bearing Gorazde registration plates and distributed among the Muslims, I can only say that Magribija mosque is not in the line of vision from the military hospital. So it's very difficult for anybody to have seen the weapons being distributed from that mosque, if they were in the hospital. They could only see that possibly happening if they were really close to the mosque.

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: You have your statement in front of you. Can we agree that Dr. Tausan doesn't say that he saw it from the hospital?

utterances.speaker: BAKIR NAKAS [Resumed]
utterances.text: "I saw when they brought the weapons in in a lorry bearing Gorazde registration plates."

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: He doesn't say that.

utterances.speaker: BAKIR NAKAS [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, he claims that he saw it from the hospital because a majority of the employees, and especially the CEO, never left the hospital. They never went for long strolls around the hospital because the Nis Specials Unit was billeted in the hospital and they controlled any movements in and out of the hospital. At one point in time I tried to enter the hospital and I was stopped at the entrance because I was not welcome.

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: Doctor, how do you know that Dr. Tausan did not leave the hospital for a month or so? And why did he not leave the hospital, if, what you claim, is true?

utterances.speaker: BAKIR NAKAS [Resumed]
utterances.text: I repeat, that that is my assumption. When I was in the hospital --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Could I -- to ask this witness to comment on matters he has no personal knowledge of and then to continue questioning on all kind of assumptions, that is not, I think, what assists the Chamber at this moment. The proper way of doing it would be to call the -- Dr. Tausan at a later stage, if there's any need to do that. Let's first ask what the witness knows and then put to him anything which is not consistent with that, to the extent he can answer those questions. But let's refrain from assumptions. Please proceed.

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I will, Your Honours. We will go back to this document.

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: But now I would like to look at paragraph 16 in your statement, which is under seal, which is P941. P941. In view of what you have just stated, and in view of the Trial Chamber's remarks, in this paragraph, you say -- we will also receive the B/C/S version, you repeat: "I was informed that the JNA, the day after I left the hospital on 8th April 1992, the JNA brought in special forces, approximately 60 men, from Nis. I believe that the JNA moved special units with equipment into the area of the hospital to attempt to prepare to cut the city in half." First of all, who informed you that the JNA had brought in approximately 60 men from Nis?

utterances.speaker: BAKIR NAKAS [Resumed]
utterances.text: I received that information from the people with whom I had worked for five, ten, or 20 years. Those who remained in the hospital and with whom I was in communication. They were all hospital employees.

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: Please don't worry, I'm waiting for the interpretation to end.

utterances.speaker: BAKIR NAKAS [Resumed]
utterances.text: I know. I know.

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: You didn't see them, did you, those men?

utterances.speaker: BAKIR NAKAS [Resumed]
utterances.text: You mean those men in uniform?

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: Of whom you heard that they were specials from Nis.

utterances.speaker: BAKIR NAKAS [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, I didn't see them until the moment when I tried to enter the military hospital. I don't know what date that was. For health reasons, I wanted to enter the hospital, but I was stopped by the regular troops whom I knew. They had consulted with men in camouflage uniforms, bearing heavier weaponry than the regular soldiers, and that made me realise that those were special units. The second time I saw those men was when I was reading reports from Skenderija, after the conflict at Skenderija between those forces and members of the Territorial Defence. I saw that report on television.

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: You say further on that you believed that the JNA moved special units into the area of the hospital to attempt to prepare to cut the city in half. What made you conclude that?

utterances.speaker: BAKIR NAKAS [Resumed]
utterances.text: That was my assumption which was based on the fact that absolutely there was no need to bring in any special units into the hospital. Because there was a platoon in the hospital that could provide full security for the hospital. All the department chiefs in the hospital were armed with automatic rifles and Skorpio rifles. That's why I thought that no such unit was needed unless somebody was planning other activities and other operations.

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: Thank you, Doctor. And now let us go back to the document that we had on the screen a little while ago, 1D778. I would like us to look at page 2, at the last paragraph. The then-CEO of the hospital, Dr. Tausan, describes that same event. But he says -- let us focus on the last lines on page 2. I'm going to read. The two of us can follow in our own language, but I want the document to be interpreted.

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Let's zoom down -- let's scroll down. I'm interested in a couple of lines at the very bottom of the page. A little bit more. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: Dr. Tausan speaks about the same events, and he says: "From that day on Muslims occasionally opened fire on the military hospital buildings, so the command of the Military District sent a group of soldiers to provide security for the hospital. I remember that there were -- were a total of 26 soldiers in the security detail. One of the most fierce sniper attacks came from the Unis building so nobody dared move around within the hospital perimeter. That was the first time that the security detail responded to the attack." This is the end of the quotation, and my question is this: Could you accept that what you heard with regard to the number of people who had been brought in to provide security for the hospital during that period of time by the Military District, as Dr. Tausan says, would be correct?

utterances.speaker: BAKIR NAKAS [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, this is what Dr. Tausan says. However, when I returned to the hospital on the 10th of May, and when I inspected the hospital, I could establish that the number of JNA members who had stayed in the hospital was higher because two complete departments, the internal diseases department and the skin diseases department, had been turned into a dormitory. There were a lot of shell case -- casings and other materiel and technical equipment there. So judging by the space that they occupied, I wouldn't say that there were only 26 of them. If Dr. Tausan says that there were 26, I cannot dispute that. But from my visual inspection, I could only say that there were more than them.

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: When you returned on the 10th of May, did you learn that during your absence, on the 3rd of May 1992 - and I'm talking about the medical records that were available to you and that you analysed - there -- there was a record made of two patients having been wounded and UNPROFOR having been informed about that. And then, on the 6th of May, 1992, did anybody register the wounding of a young girl who was being treated at the hospital, and that was four days before your return?

utterances.speaker: BAKIR NAKAS [Resumed]
utterances.text: If there were such records, they were recorded in medical histories. Those were hospitalised patients who had their own charts. Any changes were recorded in their own charts.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Let me stop you there. Do you have any recollection of such an incident being recorded which happened on the 6th of May, after you returned on the 10th of May? Do you have any recollection of it? Two patients having been wounded, one young girl.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honours, I was not at the hospital at the time. Therefore, I don't know anything about that. I did not have any information to that effect.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: You didn't learn about such a registration after you returned on the 10th of May. Is that a correct understanding of your answer?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I did not find any such records in the surgical department, but if such incidents happened, they would have been recorded in the patient's personal medical charts which are kept elsewhere.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Well, therefore, the simple answer is, no, you didn't learn about it. Please proceed, Mr. Stojanovic. Let's try to keep to facts rather than to interpretations, inferences, and conclusions. Please proceed.

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you. Just one more question.

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: When you returned on the 10th of May, Doctor, did you notice and did you take over the management of the hospital? Did you notice any damage on the admin building, on the dental surgery building, the laboratory, and the -- the -- building that housed the gynecological department?

utterances.speaker: BAKIR NAKAS [Resumed]
utterances.text: There -- no record was made of the takeover. The damage that was visible could be seen on the southern part of the central building between the seventh and eighth floors. There was a -- damage probably caused by a mortar shell or some such thing. As for any other damage that was visible on the buildings, there was some on the facade, but that could have been caused by bullets fired from close vicinity. In other words, there was no other major physical damage, save for that one big hole between the seventh and eighth floors.

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: If I understood you properly, that damage occurred while the JNA was still in the military hospital.

utterances.speaker: BAKIR NAKAS [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, that's the hit that I discussed at the beginning of my testimony.

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honours, could this be marked for identification under 1D778, pending the official translation of the document.

utterances.speaker: MS. D'ASCOLI
utterances.text: Yes, no objection, Your Honours. I just note that however we're not able to re-examine the witness or in any way having a context for this document missing the translation, but ...

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. That is clear. If any remedy is needed, we'll hear from you at a later stage. Madam Registrar.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Document 1D778 receives number D230, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: D230 is marked for identification.

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: Doctor, let us go back to the document under seal, P941, paragraph 9. Paragraph 9. I have a couple of questions to clarify your position. In your statement you say that you took over the hospital and that during the same period, you were a member of the Crisis Staff. You will see it in a minute in paragraph 9. And you say that: "The Crisis Staff was an organisation comprised of managers of all health institutions in Sarajevo who met on a daily basis to resolve all sorts of issues." My question is this: Was that an ad hoc body or was that a body that was set up pursuant to a document issued by a state body and was named the Crisis Staff?

utterances.speaker: BAKIR NAKAS [Resumed]
utterances.text: The Crisis Staff was set up sometime in April, or perhaps in March; I'm not sure. At that time I was still at the military hospital. I did not see that document pursuant to which it was set up, but I suppose that it was set up based on a law, on a regulation that was issued by a -- the authoritative body. It was not an ad hoc group. That group had its special role. I represented my hospital. I was attached to that group. And when we it comes to the structure and the setting up of the Crisis Staff, I really was not aware of any details.

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: When it comes to that Crisis Staff, was it composed only of health professionals?

utterances.speaker: BAKIR NAKAS [Resumed]
utterances.text: The Crisis Staff, most of its members were health professionals, but humanitarian workers participated in its meetings, both locals and international representatives. There are also people from the police, the armed forces, if an agenda topic required their presence. The team had its very firm structure and most of its members were health professionals, but there was a broader group which involved people who would be called as needed.

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: Why am I asking you this? What am I aiming at? There's something I want to clarify. Such a structure of the Crisis Staff, could it issue binding decisions with regard to safety, logistics, and the management of your hospital?

utterances.speaker: BAKIR NAKAS [Resumed]
utterances.text: The role of the Crisis Staff was mostly as a co-ordinating and advisory body, not vis-a-vis health care institutions but vis-a-vis ministries and authoritative bodies in the city. The proposals that they issued and the suggestions that they came up with would be sent to the authorities who transformed them into instructions and decrees that everybody had to adhere to. It did not have a major impact on the management of the institution that I managed.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honours, I would like to --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. We are close to the point where we take a break. If you could conclude and then you have 20 minutes to consult with Mr. Mladic. Have you -- has your last question been answered, Mr. Stojanovic?

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes, Your Honour. I will have just one questions that the general suggested I should put. I can complete this topic with that one question and then we can take our first break.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Please put that question to the witness.

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] But I would like to consult with the general briefly.

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: Doctor, this will be my last question on this topic. Bearing in mind the record where you said that as far as you knew it was set up in March or April, was it in 1992?

utterances.speaker: BAKIR NAKAS [Resumed]
utterances.text: It was fully functional in March and April 1992. However, one part of the Crisis Staff within the organisation of the republican public health institution, headed by Professor Smajkic functioned in 1991 already, during the period when certain activities were taking place in Croatia. There was a continuity during that period, but those things did not really concern so much Bosnia-Herzegovina and Sarajevo. The Crisis Staff became fully functional and it assumed its full role vis-a-vis health care institutions in Sarajevo at the beginning of 1992, and then it took off -- what I'm saying is that the Crisis Staff existed already in 1991.

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: Was Professor Smajkic the head of the Crisis Staff that you discuss in paragraph 9?

utterances.speaker: BAKIR NAKAS [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Maybe this is a good moment, Your Honours, to have our first break.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: We'll take a break. The witness may follow the usher.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: We will resume at ten minutes to 11.00.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Could the witness be escorted into the courtroom. Meanwhile, I use the time. That -- the Defence has requested further guidance on amendments to 65 ter summaries. And on the 1st of February of this year, in an e-mail to the parties, the Chamber requested the Prosecution's position on the Defence requests for further guidance. Namely, how much time is appropriate for amending the summary and whether statement -- the statement presumption covers all statements to be tendered through the particular witness. And the Prosecution, I think, has not yet responded. Mr. Groome.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: Your Honour, I have some notes and maybe after the next break I can address the Chamber. I think I can express our position in a minute or two.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: In a minute or two. Welcome back, Mr. Nakas. Mr. Stojanovic will now continue his cross-examination.

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: Doctor, I would like us to see again, under seal, P941 in e-court, and focus on paragraph 13. That is your statement. You describe your hospital there. I will ask you just one question about paragraph 13. Would you agree with me that the military hospital complex consisted of several separate holes? I'm talking in the terms of its construction.

utterances.speaker: BAKIR NAKAS [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. But with a note that they were all interconnected. These were architectural holes. They were separately build but their interrelations were such that they were all connected into one general hole.

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Could we now please have P3 from the Sarajevo Court Binder in e-court. We need page 6. And let us focus on this photograph, the part that could be relevant for the questions I'm about to ask you. We will see a map of Sarajevo, Doctor, and let us try to focus on the section where approximately the hospital building should be located. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: I will now ask you to use the assistance of court usher to mark with a pen the hospital building, if you can see it here.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Stojanovic, would it not be better to use this part --

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] It's a bit difficult.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: -- of the map which is -- gives more details? We have several other maps. I ...

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honours, I made an effort but I could not find a map including the area that I would like to cover with the witness and have him mark it. If it's available, I will do it with pleasure, but there are several toponyms here that -- because of which I wanted to use this particular map.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: I do not know, of course, what area you want to cover. Let's proceed.

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you in any case.

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: Doctor, I will ask you to draw a circle around the complex of the military hospital, or State Hospital, buildings at the time when you were its head.

utterances.speaker: BAKIR NAKAS [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, this map is a bit confusing for a me in a sense because there are all these colours and everything. But I suppose that the hospital facilities are here.

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: Thank you. Can you please add the letters DB so that they stand for the State Hospital or "drzavna bolna" in B/C/S, for the record.

utterances.speaker: BAKIR NAKAS [Resumed]
utterances.text: [Marks]

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: Thank you. And now, Doctor, I will ask you to draw a circle around the area in which, as you say in your statement -- actually, from which you saw that artillery fire was opened on the south wing of the hospital.

utterances.speaker: BAKIR NAKAS [Resumed]
utterances.text: It is this line ... whether it says Vrace here, I'm not sure, in this part. But this is the line across from the hospital at an elevation.

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: Doctor, can you please draw a circle around that general area which you discuss in your statement.

utterances.speaker: BAKIR NAKAS [Resumed]
utterances.text: This area would practically include ... it's somewhat difficult, because I cannot see the letters of the names of the toponyms which are included in the map. But this is the area. Now whether it was somewhat more to the south or to the north, I cannot find my bearings because I cannot decipher the place names. But, for sure, it was in this general area, across from the hospital.

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: I will also ask you now to mark, if you can see that, below the big red letters --

utterances.speaker: BAKIR NAKAS [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: -- the toponym which is called Debelo Brdo. If you can see that and if you can read it.

utterances.speaker: BAKIR NAKAS [Resumed]
utterances.text: It seems to me that it says here "Brdo," but not "Debelo." I'm not sure. Even with a lot of imagination, I cannot ... I cannot read it.

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: Can you tell us whether you know about Debelo Brdo? You're familiar with this toponym?

utterances.speaker: BAKIR NAKAS [Resumed]
utterances.text: I know the name. And I know that it's on a part of the Trebevic slope facing us. And it borders with the Jewish cemetery, somewhere up there in the direction of Osmice, or thereabouts.

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: Thank you. Can you also mark for us the area of Osmice, which you also mention in your statement.

utterances.speaker: BAKIR NAKAS [Resumed]
utterances.text: That should also be written here, but I cannot see where it is written. If I could see the word "Osmice," I could then mark it, and, as it is, I can just --

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: Well, you can draw a wider circle around the area where Osmice are located.

utterances.speaker: BAKIR NAKAS [Resumed]
utterances.text: With a lot of imagination.

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: Can I just also ask you for the purposes of marking to write a letter O in the circle around Osmice.

utterances.speaker: BAKIR NAKAS [Resumed]
utterances.text: [Marks]

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: Doctor, to your best estimate as a native of Sarajevo, what is the distance, as the crow flies?

utterances.speaker: BAKIR NAKAS [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, approximately between 3- and 400 metres.

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: Will you please tell me, Doctor, whether you are familiar with the fact that the Debelo Brdo elevation was under the control of the BH Army through -- practically throughout the war?

utterances.speaker: BAKIR NAKAS [Resumed]
utterances.text: If you say that it was, then it was. I had no need to know that it was under the control of the army.

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: Judging by your familiarity with the terrain, is it possible to see the south wing of the hospital without any obstructions from Debelo Brdo?

utterances.speaker: BAKIR NAKAS [Resumed]
utterances.text: Physically, yes. There is nothing to obstruct the view.

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: Thank you. I will also ask you to mark with a circle the location of the Magribija mosque. We talked about it during ...

utterances.speaker: BAKIR NAKAS [Resumed]
utterances.text: It's true that there were much better maps, but the Magribija mosque is here, because this white space is the old Turkish military hospital, and somewhere there, in the middle, is Magribija. It's the street connecting Kranjceviceva Street with Titova Street.

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: Could you just please mark it with MG for Magribija "dzamija" in B/C/S, the Magribija mosque. Thank you. And if you can also mark the Unis building, or, rather, the Unis facilities on this map.

utterances.speaker: BAKIR NAKAS [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, it seems that these are the two facilities. These two here.

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: Thank you. Can you please write the word "Unis" above it.

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honour, with your leave, I tender this into evidence, the map with the markings, but we'll try to bring it up once again, if that is doable.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Well, we'll deal with that soon. Could I first ask you a question. Mr. Stojanovic, you said: "As a" -- "to your best estimate as a native of Sarajevo, what is the distance, as the crow flies?" The distance between what and what? Osmice and ...

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] My question was between the area which the witness marked as the area from which the fire was coming with the big elliptical circle and the military hospital complex.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. And you apparently were satisfied with 3- to 400 metres. May I invite you to sit together with the Prosecution and perhaps not just as a native of Sarajevo but just on the scale of the map to find out what the distance is. Then, Madam Registrar, this map marked by the witness would be...

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Map from Exhibit P3, page 6, receives number D231, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: And is admitted into evidence.

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you, Your Honours. Could we now please see 1D779 in e-court.

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: Doctor, this is a photograph for which an investigator working for us on the ground told me that it was taken in May 2010 and that this is the Debelo Brdo elevation. Does your memory say anything about the claim I have just made?

utterances.speaker: BAKIR NAKAS [Resumed]
utterances.text: Even though I am a native of Sarajevo, it is a pity, but I never went up to Debelo Brdo in my whole life, so I couldn't confirm that this is the place. I never saw it looking like this.

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: All right.

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Then I would like to have a look at another photograph from the same exhibit; 1D779, photograph 2, please. That's page 2.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Your Honour -- Your Honours, there is only one photograph uploaded under this number.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Stojanovic, any other number?

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I apologise. Yes, Your Honours. 1D785.

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: Doctor, I will say this once again for the record. We claim that this is a photograph taken in May 2010 from Debelo Brdo and focussing on the section of Sarajevo where the State Hospital building is situated. What I want to ask you now is this: Judging by what you marked on the map just a while ago, could you say on the basis of this photograph whether the State Hospital building is visible in this photograph and whether this is the direction, according to your knowledge of toponyms, if this is Debelo Brdo?

utterances.speaker: BAKIR NAKAS [Resumed]
utterances.text: Absolutely. As Sarajevo is in a valley, all the elevations with which Trebevic and other mountains around Sarajevo begin would allow one to see this whole area in this way, as if it were on the palm of one's hand. So as you're moving along the road from Lukavica towards the summit of Trebevic, all along you see Sarajevo spread out on front of you as on the palm of one's hand. So I could not claim that this is the place on Debelo Brdo from which you can see the State Hospital of Sarajevo like this. Because the valley below is such that from all positions in this area it allows you to see what is depicted in this photograph.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: The witness has stated that he doesn't know exactly where Debelo Brdo is. The witness has also stated that he had never been there. Is there any dispute about the fact whether you could see from Debelo Brdo the hospital? I mean, we spent a lot of time on it.

utterances.speaker: MS. D'ASCOLI
utterances.text: Well, Your Honours, I'm not in a position of agreeing whether from Debelo Brdo. I mean, at this moment --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: No. Has it ever been explored, Mr. Stojanovic? I cannot imagine that we have to spend so much time on what seems to be a relatively simple matter. This witness has told us that he can't help us. So if it's important for you to establish, I would say get in touch with the Prosecution and establish it. Because you may well be right. Please proceed.

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you. I will finish with this area quickly.

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: I will ask just the doctor to mark with the pen the State Hospital building in this photograph.

utterances.speaker: BAKIR NAKAS [Resumed]
utterances.text: [Marks]

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: Could you please put the letters VB for "vojna bolnica," which is military hospital in B/C/S. And just a question, Doctor: Would you agree with me, that what we see here represents the south wing or the southern side of the military hospital building?

utterances.speaker: BAKIR NAKAS [Resumed]
utterances.text: That is undoubted.

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honours, I tender this photograph into evidence.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Madam Registrar.

utterances.speaker: MS. D'ASCOLI
utterances.text: Well, Your Honours, I just have an objection with regard to the fact that the description of the exhibit says a view of military hospital from Debelo Brdo, and we have not established that --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: We are not bound by any description.

utterances.speaker: MS. D'ASCOLI
utterances.text: Okay.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: What we admit into evidence is a photograph which seems of a summertime, green leaves, and we see what the witness said is a hospital.

utterances.speaker: MS. D'ASCOLI
utterances.text: Okay.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: That's the only thing we have here. Madam Registrar, photograph marked by the witness.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Receives number D232, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: D232 is admitted into evidence and should be described in a way not as to say that it is taken from Debelo Brdo. Please proceed.

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you. Could we now please have the document which is Prosecution 65 ter 261777 [as interpreted].

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Is it a six-digit number? 261777. Six digits.

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] 26177. So just five digits.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you. I think that we can see the document on the screen now. That's the one we need.

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: Doctor, I will now ask you to tell us, first of all, whether you recognise if this is the south side of the military hospital building.

utterances.speaker: BAKIR NAKAS [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, this is the facade of the central 12-storey building seen from the south.

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: Will we agree that the first three floors cannot be seen due to the obstacle that we see in the lower part of the photo?

utterances.speaker: BAKIR NAKAS [Resumed]
utterances.text: What obstacle are you talking about?

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: The lower part of the photo, you see a concrete-filled part of the building where there are no floors or at least we cannot discern them. And, on top of that, we see the remaining nine floors of the hospital.

utterances.speaker: BAKIR NAKAS [Resumed]
utterances.text: The part that you see is not discernible is actually the second floor of the hospital with the central operating area, the hollow part is the third floor, and the rest of the building from the fourth to the twelfth floors are patients' rooms.

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: In this photo, Doctor, can we see the damage that you described as having been there when you returned to the hospital in May 1992? The rest of the photo exists --

utterances.speaker: BAKIR NAKAS [Resumed]
utterances.text: Perhaps we should see that part, but I would say it would be approximately around here, it would be much better if you show the -- the other part of the photo. That area differed from the other areas of the facade for a long time.

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: Is it the area between the seventh and the eighth floors, as you told us a while ago?

utterances.speaker: BAKIR NAKAS [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: According to the best of your recollection, during the four years of war, was this part of the hospital, the southern part of the hospital, ever hit by a tank shell?

utterances.speaker: BAKIR NAKAS [Resumed]
utterances.text: Some of the hits looked like tank-shell hits, because we used to -- found remains that were similar to tank shells. I don't know which damage was inflicted by tank shells. However, based on the remains of those shells, we were able to conclude that those were tank shells.

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: In your statement, Doctor, you state that tank shells - and I'm referring to paragraph 22 in your statement - used to hit the fifth, the sixth, and the eighth floors. I'm asking you this: In view of what you stated in paragraph 22, would you be able to mark any of the damage on the south wing of the hospital that would correspond to tank-shell hits?

utterances.speaker: BAKIR NAKAS [Resumed]
utterances.text: The fifth, the sixth, the eighth floors, and there are some others, here.

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: Doctor, since you -- we will be using this document, could you put the letters TO next to the damage that you found on the 10th of May. And as for the other five circles, could you mark them with the letters TG, standing for tank shells.

utterances.speaker: BAKIR NAKAS [Resumed]
utterances.text: [Marks]

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: And now my question: You have just marked certain things. Do you know that that damage was caused by tank shells, or is it just your assumption?

utterances.speaker: BAKIR NAKAS [Resumed]
utterances.text: It is absolutely my assumption. It is not full knowledge that could arise from evidence.

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] And now, Your Honours, could we please tender this photo into evidence, and then I will show the witness another photo.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Nakas, earlier you said: "Perhaps we should see the part" -- you said, "it would be much better if you showed the other part of the photo." Now the whole of the photo was shown to you, but did you intend to say that you would like to see a photo of the whole of the southern facade of this building, also the parts which is not visible on this photo?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I'm sure that my impression would be different if I were to be shown the entire photo of the building.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. The photo of the entire building. Meanwhile, I see that the markings have disappeared. There we are. You want to tender this ... Madam Registrar.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Page 1 of document 26177 as marked by the witness receives number D233, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: D233 is admitted into evidence. Mr. Stojanovic, if the witness says that he could give better answers by viewing the whole of the southern wall -- of the southern facade of the building, it's better to give him an opportunity to do so rather than to just ignore his wish. Please proceed.

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you, Your Honours, I'll do my best. I'm looking for the best possible photo, with no ill intentions. I would to call up 65 ter 26227. Because I believe that this is the only photo depicting the entire south wing of the hospital. I'd like to call up page 8. This photo was taken on the 1st October, 1995, and we found this photo in the Prosecutor's collection of documents.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: At this moment we appear to see the back of a photograph which is not very helpful.

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] ERN is 0003 --

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Could the -- could Mr. Stojanovic please repeat the ERN number.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Could you please repeat the ERN number. And Ms. D'Ascoli is on her feet as well.

utterances.speaker: MS. D'ASCOLI
utterances.text: Yes, Your Honours. If I can give assistance. In the rest of the exhibit marked with the 65 ter 26177, page 2 of the document shows the remaining -- the other part of the south facade. Now, I don't see in the exhibit that we have photos of the entire building from -- I mean, the other sides. But if Dr. Nakas then would prefer to see the fuller side, meaning the whole southern side, this is visible, the second half of that side, from page 2.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: What I see, as a matter of fact, that page 1 depicts part of the facade, and we do not know which part; page 2 is, again, the back side. But let's -- let's first focus on the questions Mr. Stojanovic wants to put to the witness.

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honours, I believe that I will be able to follow your instructions, and I would like to call up -- call up 559. Now we're looking at 556. And I would like to call up P559. Thank you. I believe that this is the photograph that I wanted to show the witness.

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: Doctor, I don't think that we have been able to locate a better photo. I believe that this is the entire south wing. Do you agree?

utterances.speaker: BAKIR NAKAS [Resumed]
utterances.text: I can see the best part of the building now. We did not see it before. One part was -- was missing in the other photo, but it's not that important.

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: The damage that you have just marked, how was that inflicted; do you know?

utterances.speaker: BAKIR NAKAS [Resumed]
utterances.text: Again, I'm a doctor, so this is just my assumption. Judging by the destructive effects, it could have been either a heavy mortar or a tank.

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: And now I'm going to ask you to put the letter O, standing for damage, next to your markings.

utterances.speaker: BAKIR NAKAS [Resumed]
utterances.text: [Marks]

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: Doctor, in view of the previous photograph and this photo, can you spot any regularities in the damage that you marked?

utterances.speaker: BAKIR NAKAS [Resumed]
utterances.text: The principal regularity is the fact that the shells hit the area where patients' rooms are. The hits were from the fifth to the ninth floors; whereas, the second, the third, the fourth, the twelfth, and the eleventh floors were less impacted. If you analyse the entire surface of the wall, you will see that most of the hits are visible in the right-hand side part and in the central part of the southern facade.

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: Could you please mark --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes, please, continue with the marking and then -- You'd like the witness to mark what?

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: Doctor, can you put a vertical line across the middle of the building? That would allow us to analyse your words better.

utterances.speaker: BAKIR NAKAS [Resumed]
utterances.text: [Marks]

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Do you mean vertical to the building or top down on the photograph? What is your intention?

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] The middle of the building. A vertical line through the building.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I believe that this would be pretty much accurate.

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: Thank you, Doctor.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Well, whatever that brings us, but we'll see that in a minute. Mr. Stojanovic, first of all, I think all the Judges heard the "regularity" of the damage, but apart from regularity or irregularity, as it is said here, and which you may have used in your own language, the Judges have got no idea what a regularity or irregularity of damage is. Are you seeking for a pattern and, if so, what kind of a pattern? What is a regularity or irregularity of damage? If you could tell us, then we might be better able to understand the evidence.

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes, Your Honour. Maybe it's a problem in terminology.

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: All my questions are based on the answer that you previously gave us. Do you agree with me that the south-east --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Stojanovic, I am asking you what your words mean, because for us to understand the evidence, we'd like to know what the words stand for: What is regularity, what is irregularity of damage? What's the regularity of a car? I wouldn't know. Please tell us what -- what you wanted to ask. Rephrase the question in such a way that we understand what it is about.

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I will, Your Honours. Although, I don't understand. I did not use the word regularity. That's why I'm a bit confused.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Then please rephrase your question or put it again in such a way that it is clear to us what you've asked the witness.

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Very well.

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: Sir, Doctor, I apologise. Do you agree with me that the focus of all the hits was in the south-west -- southeastern part of the building?

utterances.speaker: BAKIR NAKAS [Resumed]
utterances.text: All of these are photos of the southern side, which may give us an impression that only that side was hit. However, the other parts of the building were also hit as well as the roof and other buildings which are lower than this central building. But, in physical terms, one could say that most of the hits are on the southern side with a slight aberration towards the eastern part of the building.

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: And now could you please pay attention to the third row from the bottom. I hope you can see it. And the damage of -- in the third row.

utterances.speaker: BAKIR NAKAS [Resumed]
utterances.text: To the left or to the right?

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: To the right from the vertical line. According to your knowledge, what was this damage caused by?

utterances.speaker: BAKIR NAKAS [Resumed]
utterances.text: I underline the fact that I don't know as much as to be able to give you a precise answer, which is why my answers are not very categorical. I would like just to emphasise one fact. This photo taken from this angle does not really illustrate the scope of a damage inside of the building, because there are rooms in that building that no longer existed. These are the exterior parts and they are what they are, but the interior damage was --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Could I stop you there. That was not asked, whether this depicts the damage to the inside of the building. It clearly does not. If there are any questions about that, Mr. Stojanovic will put them to you. Mr. Stojanovic, please, clear question.

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes, Your Honour. I would like to tender this photo which has been marked by the witness, and then I will move on to another topic.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Thank you. Madam Registrar, the number would be ...

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Document 26227, page 15, as marked by witness, receives number D234, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: D234 is admitted into evidence. Mr. Stojanovic, could I ask you just in order to better understand the testimony, did you want to draw the attention of the Chamber to the fact that most of the damage visible on this photograph is on the right part rather than on the left part of the building? Is that what you intended to draw our intention to? One simple question would have done. Is --

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes, Your Honour. Thank you very much. The right-hand side, which we said was the eastern side.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. Well, it's all south. But the -- now, is there any suggestion that, therefore, the damage must have been caused from projectiles coming from the east? Or what does it tell us? I mean, what is the suggestion underlying these questions?

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] The substance of what we are trying to put is the position advanced by our expert would establish in relation to Debelo Brdo, as we indicated previously. And it has to do with this side of the building.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: So -- so, if I understand you well, what you are trying to establish at this moment, that, if the damage is to the right side of the southern face of the building, that then it's more likely that it came from Debelo Brdo. Is that --

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] That's correct, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Well, then we know what to consider when listening to the evidence. Please proceed.

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you for your assistance. Can we now look at 1D781.

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: Doctor, we will now see a photograph in e-court depicting the interior.

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honours, this is a photograph we received from the collection of photographs of the Prosecution from a different case.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Your Honours, this is not in e-court.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: I do understand that it's not in e-court. Mr. Stojanovic, has it been uploaded? If not, you can move on and then after the next break we'll see whether the photograph is in e-court, yes or no. You may proceed.

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Very well. Let's check if we have in e-court 1D782. 782. This is the photograph, 1D782. Your Honours, let me just say that the photograph was taken in a different case. It was one of the photographs from a collection of photographs used by the Prosecution in that case.

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: Doctor, do you recognise the inside of one of the rooms in the State Hospital?

utterances.speaker: BAKIR NAKAS [Resumed]
utterances.text: Judging by the window-frames, the chairs, and the furniture in general, this would have been one of the rooms in the State Hospital set aside for rest.

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: Doctor, can you explain to us how is it possible that this shell [as interpreted], which sits literally beneath a portion of the facade which is clearly damaged should be in such an intact and pristine condition?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Could we first establish which shell you are referring to. Is there -- Could we first ask the witness whether he sees any shell in this picture? Or was it in one of the other pictures?

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Interpreter's correction: A shelf, sorry.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Then a shelf. That is -- explains, perhaps, a lot. We understood "shell," whereas the interpreters intended to say "shelf." Yes.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Shelf.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Which shelf are you referring to? Are you referring to the shelf just below -- below the window to the left of the room? Seen from the position of the photographer?

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] That's correct, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] If you're asking me to explain how come this shell or chest should be in such good condition, the only explanation would be that it had been knocked over and was then perhaps placed upward again. Otherwise, the debris from this opening of the facade would have had to have been on it.

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you very much. Your Honours, can this photograph be admitted into evidence.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Madam Registrar.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Document 1D782 receives number D235, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: MS. D'ASCOLI
utterances.text: Your Honours, can I just ask Mr. Stojanovic which is the previous case he mentioned where this set of photographs was used? Just for the record and so that we can check. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honour, the document was used in the case against General Stanislav Galic and carries Prosecution markings, ET9829, and it was taken by John Ashton, a representative of the Prosecution. The marking is IT9829.

utterances.speaker: MS. D'ASCOLI
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. D235 is admitted into evidence.

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you. My information is that the document, 1D781, is now uploaded in e-court. Can we call it up for the doctor to have a look at it.

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: Doctor --

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] If I may get a moment, Your Honours, to consult.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Well, the rule is that you consult during the breaks. If there's any -- and that Mr. Mladic sends a little note. We've noticed that more frequently now, the basic rule, which, of course, no exceptions, is not kept. We would rather be a bit strict on that. Please proceed.

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: Doctor, we have another photograph from the same collection on our screens. Judging by the photograph and what can be seen out of this room, can you tell us which floor this might be and what room this is?

utterances.speaker: BAKIR NAKAS [Resumed]
utterances.text: This is a six-bed room for patients. I know that it would normally fit six beds in here. I can recognise the -- the bearings that I see here and the frame, and I may even have commented on the external appearance of this room when I said that the damage to the inside was much more extensive than could be seen from the outside.

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: Exactly. That was exactly what I wanted to ask you. Do you agree with me that the space between the two windows was constructed of brick blocks, parts of which we can see in the middle of the photograph?

utterances.speaker: BAKIR NAKAS [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: Do you agree with me that in that part of the wall, there is no reinforced concrete structure?

utterances.speaker: BAKIR NAKAS [Resumed]
utterances.text: None that I can see in the photograph. But I do assume that there must be parts of reinforced concrete either in the bottom part or in the -- in the area close to the ceiling -- I'm sorry. Though I'm not sure. It must have been somehow connected, but whether there was any sort of reinforced concrete there, I'm not sure.

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: You said that this was a room that would fit six beds. Would these beds have been taken out earlier, since they're not here?

utterances.speaker: BAKIR NAKAS [Resumed]
utterances.text: As of the 13th of May, when the shelling started, we decided that all the patients should be taken down to the basement where there were thicker walls. Most of the furnishings were also taken elsewhere, to the corridors, dressing rooms, the gym.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
